title: Throughput-coordinated prefetch controller for mixed-length streams
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: For mixed prompt/response length workloads (customer chat, search+followups), our continuous batching scheduler over-prefetches KV pages for long-tail sessions and under-serves short, latency-sensitive turns. This causes two correlated issues: (1) KV cache residency swings (hot entries evicted prematurely) and (2) GPU slab fragmentation leading to degraded p99 latency under load.

Goal: Implement a throughput-coordinated prefetch controller (TCPC) that biases KV prefetch windows and batch admission by per-session throughput budget and a lightweight session occupancy histogram. TCPC should reduce unnecessary KV warming for low-throughput long contexts and prioritize short-turn latency by limiting slot tenure for low-probability long continuations.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a per-session throughput estimator (exponential moving average of tokens/s and average turn length) used to compute a prefetch budget.
- Replace fixed prefetch horizon with a dynamic horizon: horizon = base_horizon * f(throughput, recent_length_variance). Low throughput -> smaller horizon.
- Tie prefetch actions to KV watermarks and a slab-rebalancer signal: only prefetch if KV_residency < target_residency and slab_fragmentation < fragmentation_threshold, otherwise defer and mark session as low-prefetch.
- Implement a conservative fallback: when contention is high, TCPC will preferentially preserve prefixes for high-throughput sessions and shift low-throughput long sessions to a cold-path (read-from-storage-on-demand) to avoid catastrophic eviction churn.
- Add lightweight telemetry to measure occupancy histograms, prefetch hit rate, eviction churn, and slab fragmentation per-GPU.

Why this is different: instead of tuning admission by length bins alone, TCPC coordinates prefetch and admission decisions with throughput signals and GPU memory health metrics (watermarks + fragmentation). This reduces thrash and gives predictable p99 for latency-sensitive short turns while bounding cost for long-tail contexts.
acceptance_criteria: p50 latency for short-turn (<16 tokens prompt) workloads stays within 5% of baseline under 80th percentile load
p99 latency for mixed-length production trace improves by >=10% or remains flat with <=5% cost increase
KV prefetch hit-rate for high-throughput sessions increases by >=8% on average
GPU slab fragmentation metric decreases 10% vs. current scheduler under the mixed workload simulation
No regression in unit token-cost for the majority (>90%) of customers; documented trade-offs for long, low-throughput sessions
tasks: Design: define throughput estimator signal and tuning knobs (base_horizon, throughput_thresholds, fragmentation_threshold)
Runtime: implement per-session throughput EMA and dynamic prefetch horizon in continuous scheduler (C++)
KV layer: add prefetch gating by KV_residency and watermark feedback loop
Memory manager: expose slab_fragmentation metric and API to mark GPUs as 'constrained'
Simulations: build mixed-trace microbench harness (python) that replays production traces with controlled throughput and length distributions
Perf: run A/B on canary pool and collect latency/eviction metrics (dashboard link)
Docs: add runbook and recommended knob settings for Dedicated/Private customers
design_decisions: Use EMA(α=0.2) for throughput to respond within tens of seconds while avoiding churn
Favor preservation of hot prefixes for sessions with sustained token/s > 0.8 * GPU_avg_session_throughput
Cold-path read (on-demand streaming from backing store) is preferable to aggressive prefetch when slab_fragmentation > 0.25
Keep prefetch horizon capped (max_horizon=1024 tokens) to avoid excessive KV warm-up costs
Expose three knob tiers: conservative (default), balanced, aggressive (for throughput-optimized workloads)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike prototyped: throughput EMA added, dynamic horizon computed in scheduler simulator. Observed 12% reduction in unnecessary prefetches on public mixed trace sample.
2026-03-04: KV team added residency API; initial gating tests show prefetch deferral reduces eviction churn by ~9% in simulator.
2026-03-06: Memory manager hook for slab_fragmentation metric merged to staging branch; need integration test on multi-GPU host.

2026-03-08: Early canary rollout plan drafted. Identified two risk cases: (A) bursty chat bots that toggle throughput rapidly, (B) enterprise customers with pinned huge-context sessions. Mitigation: hysteresis on horizon changes + per-customer opt-out of cold-path.
2026-03-10: Implemented telemetry counters and dashboard tile: tcpc/prefetch_hits, tcpc/eviction_churn, tcpc/horizon_distribution. Running 24h canary on pool-beta-3.
comments: Arjun Patel (2026-03-03): Reviewed initial prototype; suggested adding slab_fragmentation threshold to avoid prefetch storms during GC cycles.
Priya Nair (PM, 2026-03-05): Flagged two enterprise customers with long pinned contexts — will coordinate opt-out flow in Console.
Luis Gomez (SRE, 2026-03-07): Requesting canary metrics include GPU mem fragmentation and page-fault rates; added to dashboard requirements.
Maya Chen (creator, 2026-03-10): Note: if canary shows regression for >2 enterprise customers, we'll pause rollout and enable per-customer opt-out by default until additional heuristics are added.
